content.text:
The `git log -L` trace on the affected lines shows a clean, direct lineage: the bug-fixing commit (9caec286) reverts to `maxSizeBeforeFirstWrap = bufferSize` / `maxSizeAfterFirstWrap = bufferSize` as defaults and only applies the frame-alignment calculation when `readSize < bufferSize` (and the aligned size is still `>= readSize`). The exact code that was removed/guarded is the code that was originally added in commit `004ec65b0c329e37ea592c764fd48f9ab9a44fe1`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 004ec65b0c329e37ea592c764fd48f9ab9a44fe1

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I used `git log -L 209,225:src/jpcsp/HLE/modules/sceAtrac3plus.java` starting at the fix commit to trace the full history of the exact lines touched by the fix (the `setHalfwayBuffer` method's `maxSizeBeforeFirstWrap`/`maxSizeAfterFirstWrap` computation). This showed every commit that ever modified those specific lines, in reverse chronological order.

**(2) The introducing change:** Commit `004ec65b` (Dec 12, 2018) changed:
```java
inputBuffer = new pspFileBuffer(addr, bufferSize, readSize, readSize);
```
to:
```java
int maxSizeBeforeFirstWrap = bufferSize - ((bufferSize - info.inputFileDataOffset) % info.atracBytesPerFrame);
int maxSizeAfterFirstWrap = bufferSize - (bufferSize % info.atracBytesPerFrame);
inputBuffer = new pspFileBuffer(addr, maxSizeBeforeFirstWrap, maxSizeAfterFirstWrap, readSize, readSize);
```
This unconditionally aligns the wrap size down to a multiple of `atracBytesPerFrame`. The bug: when `readSize` equals `bufferSize` (i.e., the buffer is already fully populated — a case the surrounding comment in the fix commit explicitly calls out), this alignment can shrink `maxSizeBeforeFirstWrap`/`maxSizeAfterFirstWrap` below `readSize`, producing an inconsistent/too-small wrap boundary for a buffer that's already full, corrupting the ATRAC3+ input buffer state (leading to bad audio decode/streaming behavior, per the issue this fix presumably addresses).

**(3) Evidence:** The fix commit `9caec286` directly reintroduces `bufferSize` as the safe default and only opts into the frame-aligned calculation when `readSize < bufferSize` AND the aligned value is still `>= readSize` — i.e., it adds exactly the guard that was missing from `004ec65b`'s original unconditional alignment logic.
